Well, just a few months later, she got married in September, just a few months later, in February of 2001, I got a horrific telephone call in the middle of the night. A raging fire had ripped through their apartment complex and both my son-in-law and my grandson had been killed in that apartment fire. And so as I began to ask God my own questions, you know, why did something like this happen? Why? Why take my grandson at such an early age? I mean, I've been a Christian since I was about 10 years old when I came to know Christ. And so I had those natural questions. And for a long time, God did not answer my question. My grandson loved him. I grew to respect him. My daughter loved him. And I said, you know, we need to find these young men. that are going to be fathers because every time a young girl comes up pregnant out of wedlock, there's a young boy out there that's going to be a dad. And in many cases, the boys get, they get sidetracked. They get pushed to the side. Her parents, they don't want to have anything to do with him because, you know, he's sort of, he's picked the flower before it's fully bloomed. And so in many cases, the young boys just fade off and fade away and leaving that young girl to have that baby and be a single mom or give it up for adoption or worse yet pursue an abortion. And so I said, we need to get these young men and raise them up to be fathers because they can do that. They don't even if they don't marry the birth mother, they still have a role and a responsibility in the life of that child. And we should, as a society, teach them how to fulfill that role. And that's where the genesis of the book came from. Because I think if we can do anything for these young mothers that are single moms, give them a willing participant, a father, a birth father, that understands what their role is. And let's start putting our society back together because the attack on the family by the culture around us these days, it's had a devastating effect. on American families. And we need to get dads understanding what their roles are.
